title: Zephyrine and the Asset
premise: Casper Nystrom, a disgraced intelligence analyst scraping by on deniable freelance work, is hired to trace the disappearance of Flight 4471 from every database in Europe — while the plane is still airborne. He discovers the jet carries 'the Asset,' a defector whose memory holds proof that a powerful consortium manufactured its own legitimacy through fabricated history, and that erasing the flight is the consortium's way of erasing him. Hunted by both the consortium and the agencies that once discarded him, Casper must decide whether to sell the Asset's secret to save himself or expose it and burn what's left of his life. In the end he chooses exposure, trading his own survival for the truth: the Asset dies, the flight stays erased for the world, but Casper smuggles the memory out — at the cost of everything he was.
about_author: Odile Coldharbour is the pen name of a former aviation-industry archivist who spent a decade cataloguing records she was never allowed to read. She writes thrillers about paper trails, vanished people, and the quiet violence of institutions.

chapters.title: The Unattributable Man
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Broke and blacklisted after three agency dismissals, Casper takes a cash job from a fixer named Voss: find out why Flight 4471 has ceased to exist in every manifest, radar log, and booking system while still broadcasting a transponder. The beat is weary competence masking desperation; he takes the case because no one else will have him.

chapters.title: Ghost Altitude
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Following the transponder to a private strip outside Riga, Casper finds the hangar scrubbed, the crew gone, and one survivor: a woman calling herself Ilse who claims to be the flight's purser and remembers passengers who don't exist. Emotional beat: first vertigo of doubt — his own records begin showing gaps too.

chapters.title: Ilse Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. We learn Ilse is not crew but the Asset herself, wearing a stolen identity, carrying memorized documents detailing the consortium's founding fraud. She tests Casper with fragments of truth. Beat: wary intimacy between two people who cannot afford to trust, sharpened by her fear of being remembered wrong.

chapters.title: Three Agencies, One Grave
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Digging into who ordered the erasure, Casper finds his old employers' fingerprints — including evidence his third dismissal was engineered to make him pliable. A former colleague warns him off, then turns up dead. Beat: rage curdling into purpose; the personal betrayal converts a job into a vendetta.

chapters.title: The Consortium's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Flashback chapter: how the consortium rewrote its origins decades ago, and how Ilse came to carry the true ledger in her head after they killed everyone else who knew it. Beat: grief and resolve; she explains the price of survival is being hunted by people who need you forgotten.

chapters.title: Buyer's Market
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Voss reveals the real client: a consortium broker offering Casper redemption, money, and reinstatement if he delivers Ilse. Cornered, Casper pretends to negotiate while planning escape. Beat: moral corrosion — he can feel how easy it would be to say yes, and hates that he's tempted.

chapters.title: Runway Nine
chapters.summary: POV alternating tight third. The handoff goes wrong; consortium cleaners hit the meet, Voss is killed, and Casper and Ilse flee across frozen farmland toward a chartered escape. Beat: kinetic terror and reluctant partnership solidifying into loyalty neither will name.

chapters.title: What Memory Is Worth
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Trapped in a safehouse, Ilse offers Casper an out: recite the ledger from her dictation, sell it independently, vanish rich. He realizes any copy he carries makes him a target forever. Beat: the book's moral crux — survival versus truth, priced out loud between two exhausted people.

chapters.title: Erasure
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. The consortium corners them; Ilse chooses to surrender herself as bait so Casper can transmit the ledger to a hundred inboxes worldwide. Her final act is making Casper promise to remember it correctly. Beat: sacrificial climax — she reclaims power by choosing what is done with her memory.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Weeks later, the ledger leaks fragment by fragment; the flight officially never existed, and no record names Casper anywhere — which is exactly how he survives. Standing in a archive reading room watching the truth surface under other people's bylines, he accepts anonymity as both punishment and inheritance. Beat: bittersweet resolution — the price of survival paid in full, memory kept alive off the record.
